div.head: ECf retr Rb XL
div.ab:
Quomodo sanctus rex Edwardus propter nequitiam et iniquitatem gentis sue et maxime propter insolentiam et superbiam filiorum comitis Godwini Willelmum
ducem heredem regni sui fecit, eo quod de Edgaro facere nequiuit.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 671–672 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

This is one of the chapter headings (rubrics) that a later writer, whom Liebermann calls “Rubricator II” and dates 1163–1189, made for the Retractator’s text; so the date given for ECf retr (c. 1140–59) does not apply to it. Liebermann prints them on pp. 670–672 as an appendix (Anhang) to ECf retr; they are numbered here “Rb” with his Roman numerals. He prints in small type what is taken from the text of ECf retr, so the words in bold are the Rubricator’s own.
Liebermann gives in the margin, in square brackets, the chapter of ECf retr that this heading belongs to: 35, 2.
Liebermann puts note 54 on the numeral; here it stands at the start of the heading. His numbering of the notes starts again at 1 on p. 672.

div.ab: How the holy King Edward, because of the wickedness and iniquity of his people and above all because of the insolence and pride of the sons of Earl Godwine, made Duke William heir of his kingdom, since he could not do so with Edgar.
